review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

1:1.sourceText: Πολυμερῶς καὶ πολυτρόπως πάλαι ὁ Θεὸς λαλήσας τοῖς πατράσιν ἐν τοῖς προφήταις
1:1.targetText: In many parts and many ways, God, having spoken long ago to the fathers by the prophets,

groups.note: The actual adverb πολυμερῶς expresses speaking in many portions/parts; LSV expands that one adverb as In many parts without independent source in, many, or parts tokens.
The actual adverb πολυτρόπως expresses speaking in many ways; the English many-ways phrase belongs to that one adverb.
Greek ἐν with the prophets expresses the means/agency of speaking; LSV renders by the prophets, retaining the actual preposition relation in this clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

1:2.sourceText: ἐπ’ ἐσχάτου τῶν ἡμερῶν τούτων ἐλάλησεν ἡμῖν ἐν Υἱῷ, ὃν ἔθηκεν κληρονόμον πάντων, δι’ οὗ καὶ ἐποίησεν τοὺς αἰῶνας·
1:2.targetText: in these last days speaks to us in [His] Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, through whom He also made the ages;

groups.note: N1904 ἐλάλησεν is aorist He spoke, while LSV uses present speaks. The actual speaking head remains linked with this tense rendering difference explicit.

1:3.sourceText: ὃς ὢν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ, φέρων τε τὰ πάντα τῷ ῥήματι τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ, καθαρισμὸν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ποιησάμενος ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τῆς Μεγαλωσύνης ἐν ὑψηλοῖς,
1:3.targetText: who being the brightness of the glory, and the impress of His subsistence, bearing up also all things by the saying of His might—having made a cleansing of our sins through Himself, sat down at the right hand of the Greatness in the highest,

groups.note: The actual noun χαρακτήρ denotes an imprint/exact representation; LSV impress is that older noun sense, not an act of impressing someone.
The actual ὑπόστασις noun designates underlying substance/being in this clause; LSV subsistence retains that head rather than a different Greek existence or image noun.
The actual substantival right-side adjective δεξιᾷ identifies the right-hand place; English expands it as the right hand without a separately printed Greek hand noun.
The actual substantival high-places adjective ὑψηλοῖς is rendered the highest; no separately written place noun is invented.

1:4.sourceText: τοσούτῳ κρείττων γενόμενος τῶν ἀγγέλων ὅσῳ διαφορώτερον παρ’ αὐτοὺς κεκληρονόμηκεν ὄνομα.
1:4.targetText: having become so much better than the messengers, as He inherited a more excellent name than them.

groups.note: The actual comparative κρείττων governs the genitive messengers; English better than states that comparison without an independently printed Greek than word.

1:5.sourceText: Τίνι γὰρ εἶπέν ποτε τῶν ἀγγέλων Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε; καὶ πάλιν Ἐγὼ ἔσομαι αὐτῷ εἰς Πατέρα, καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται μοι εἰς Υἱόν;
1:5.targetText: For to which of the messengers did He ever say, “You are My Son—today I have begotten You?” And again, “I will be to Him for a Father, and He will be to Me for a Son?”

1:6.sourceText: ὅταν δὲ πάλιν εἰσαγάγῃ τὸν πρωτότοκον εἰς τὴν οἰκουμένην, λέγει Καὶ προσκυνησάτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες ἄγγελοι Θεοῦ.
1:6.targetText: And when again He may bring the firstborn into the world, He says, “And let them worship Him—all messengers of God”;

groups.note: The actual substantivized inhabited-world designation οἰκουμένην is rendered world; its original head remains distinct from the different noun κόσμος.

1:7.sourceText: καὶ πρὸς μὲν τοὺς ἀγγέλους λέγει Ὁ ποιῶν τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ πνεύματα, καὶ τοὺς λειτουργοὺς αὐτοῦ πυρὸς φλόγα·
1:7.targetText: and to the messengers, indeed, He says, “The [One] who is making His messengers spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire”;

groups.note: The actual article nominalizes the following making participle, rendered The One who; bracketed One and relative who express that real substantival construction, not additional Greek person words.

1:8.sourceText: πρὸς δὲ τὸν Υἱόν Ὁ θρόνος σου ὁ Θεὸς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος, καὶ ἡ ῥάβδος τῆς εὐθύτητος ῥάβδος τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ.
1:8.targetText: but to the Son: “Your throne, O God, [is] throughout the age of the age; The scepter of righteousness [is the] scepter of Your kingdom;

groups.note: The articular nominative God is used as direct address in the quoted clause; LSV makes that address explicit as O God. This retains the complete written designation, not an independent Greek O particle.

Actual genitive article and uprightness/righteousness noun jointly supply of ... righteousness as the scepter qualifier. The actual euthytes head remains distinct from dikaiosyne. The actual uprightness/equity noun εὐθύτης is rendered righteousness; this is not the different δικαιοσύνη noun printed in the following verse.
Actual genitive article and kingdom noun jointly supply of ... kingdom as the second scepter qualifier. The existing His/Your source-witness possessive gaps remain unchanged.

1:10.sourceText: καί Σὺ κατ’ ἀρχάς, Κύριε, τὴν γῆν ἐθεμελίωσας, καὶ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν σού εἰσιν οἱ οὐρανοί·
1:10.targetText:
and, “You, LORD, founded the earth at the beginning,
And the heavens are a work of Your hands.

groups.note: The κατά plus beginnings time expression is rendered at the beginning; the plural source noun participates in the one English temporal idiom.
N1904 has plural works, ἔργα; LSV gives singular a work for the same actual work/result head, with the number difference explicit.

1:11.sourceText: αὐτοὶ ἀπολοῦνται, σὺ δὲ διαμένεις· καὶ πάντες ὡς ἱμάτιον παλαιωθήσονται,
1:11.targetText:
These will perish, but You remain,
And all will become old as a garment,

groups.note: The actual third-person plural αὐτοί refers back to the created heavens/earth; LSV identifies that same set as These, without changing the original pronoun into a Greek demonstrative.
The actual aging passive verb παλαιωθήσονται is expanded as will become old; its English become/old pieces do not imply separately written source words.

1:12.sourceText: καὶ ὡσεὶ περιβόλαιον ἑλίξεις αὐτούς, ὡς ἱμάτιον καὶ ἀλλαγήσονται· σὺ δὲ ὁ αὐτὸς εἶ καὶ τὰ ἔτη σου οὐκ ἐκλείψουσιν.
1:12.targetText:
And You will roll them together as a mantle, and they will be changed,
But You are the same, and Your years will not fail.”

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness comparison addition: N1904 repeats like a garment, ὡς ἱμάτιον, with the ensuing being-changed clause. LSV follows the shorter wording without that second simile. Its earlier as a mantle belongs to the separate rolling-up comparison and keeps its own actual source phrase.

1:13.sourceText: πρὸς τίνα δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων εἴρηκέν ποτε Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου;
1:13.targetText:
And to which of the messengers did He ever say, “Sit at My right hand,
Until I may make Your enemies Your footstool?”

groups.note: The actual substantival right-side designation δεξιῶν is expressed as right hand; it does not create a separately written Greek hand noun.
The until conjunction and modal particle ἕως ἄν jointly mark the open future limit; English Until retains the construction while the subjunctive predicate is rendered I may make.

Greek footstool of the feet is condensed into the one English compound footstool. The actual footstool noun, article and feet noun jointly retain that complete image, with the separately written feet possessor still anchored as the second Your.

1:14.sourceText: οὐχὶ πάντες εἰσὶν λειτουργικὰ πνεύματα εἰς διακονίαν ἀποστελλόμενα διὰ τοὺς μέλλοντας κληρονομεῖν σωτηρίαν;
1:14.targetText: Are they not all spirits of service—being sent forth for ministry because of those about to inherit salvation?

groups.note: The actual service/ministry adjective λειτουργικά qualifies spirits; LSV renders it as of service, not as an independent Greek service noun.

Greek διά with these people identifies those for whose sake the spirits are sent; LSV because of retains that person-directed relation, without changing the actual preposition into a different Greek beneficiary marker.
